title: Mixed-anion engineering of ASnS 2 O (A = Ba, Sr, Ca): first-principles insights into structure–property tuning and water-redox band-edge screening
content: Mixed-anion engineering provides a route to tune coupled structural and functional properties in Sn-based oxysulfides. Using density functional theory (GGA-PBE), we investigate ASnS2O (A = Ba, Sr, Ca) with a common ordered S/O substitution motif and selected alternative configurations. Structural relaxation yields triclinic P1 structures, with unit-cell volumes decreasing by 11.6% from 446.001 Å3 (Ba) to 394.341 Å3 (Ca). The primary configurations exhibit indirect band gaps of 1.461, 1.727, and 1.928 eV, respectively, while alternative anion orderings produce substantial variations. Fixed-volume calculations and Mulliken overlap populations indicate that volume contraction alone cannot explain band-gap widening. The valence-band edges are predominantly S/O-p-derived, whereas the conduction-band edges are mainly Sn-derived. Polycrystalline-averaged optical spectra reveal absorption maxima of 3.04 × 105, 2.35 × 105, and 2.56 × 105 cm−1 at 18.8, 23.6, and 27.8 eV, respectively, beyond the visible region. Positive-definite elastic stiffness matrices support elastic mechanical stability, although mechanical responses are non-monotonic and strain-sensitive; CaSnS2O exhibits the highest calculated hardness (6.148 GPa). Sn-5p PBE+U calculations preserve the band-gap ordering without establishing absolute-gap accuracy. At pH = 0, nominal PBE–Mulliken estimates indicate a qualitative improvement in water-redox band-edge alignment from Ba to Ca, with BaSnS2O closest to the oxidation threshold. However, the configurations lie above selected competing decomposition assemblages, and Γ-point phonon calculations cannot establish full dynamical stability. Further assessment of phase stability, absolute band edges, carrier transport, and surface kinetics is required before practical photocatalytic feasibility can be established.
